A dedicated post-closing modeling call to help analysts model the combined business after the April 1, 2025 Alani Nu close - technical, disciplined and execution-focused; management explicitly declined to provide a revenue outlook for either Alani Nu or core Celsius.

Strategic rationale: a leading better-for-you functional lifestyle platform at the intersection of consumer megatrends; Alani Nu (founded 2018, #4 US energy drink) is female-centric and complementary to gender-neutral, performance-driven Celsius - 90%+ of Alani's social followers are female.
Combined business is a strong #3 in US energy at ~16% share and ~$2B 2024 pro forma revenue; more than 90% RTD energy; Alani adds RTD protein, pre-workout, supplements.
Alani Nu's 2023-2024 P&L profile mirrors Celsius's 2022-2023 profile; gross margin moved from 40% into the low 40s, expected to converge to Celsius's profile over a 24-month supply-chain integration.

Purchase-accounting noise: ~$15M inventory step-up (opening inventory $15M higher on April 1; ~80% to Q2, ~20% to Q3; ~1% FY gross-margin drag); customer-list amortization adds ~1% in SG&A; brand/trademark assets and goodwill recorded but not amortized monthly - evaluated annually.
Interest expense ~$19M/quarter (~$57M FY) begins Q2 2025 on $900M debt at a 7.5% assumed rate; the variable SOFR+325bps rate fluctuates with SOFR quarter-to-quarter.

Scanner-vs-GAAP reconciliation is 'tricky' and 'contingent on how successful our LTOs are' - Alani recognizes GAAP revenue on delivery while Circana captures register scans; LTO launches cause pipe-fill that shifts revenue between periods (spike then fade); converges over a longer period.

$50M run-rate synergies driven mostly by headcount (using hundreds of commercial team members to absorb sales/merchandising/key-accounts/field-marketing); full run rate (~$4.2M/month) reached April 2026; only $5-10M captured across Q4 2025/Q1 2026 - most in 2026.
24-month integration with majority of work in the first 12 months, running alongside a 12-month TSA with Congo Brands; separate brand/marketing teams maintained to preserve each brand's voice.

Core Celsius got off to a slow Q1 start but is showing week-over-week growth and stabilization; a more balanced 2025 innovation cadence and summer marketing investment; the portfolio enables a branded go-to-market approach on pricing, promotion and architecture.

Alani Nu Q1 2025 was up 65-70% YoY (consolidated), partly inflated by the Sherbet Swirl LTO pipe-fill - which was briefly the #1 energy SKU at certain large retailers; consolidated growth ran +39% Q3 2024, +53% Q4 2024 (holiday-edition launch); Q2 2025 scanner data 'pretty solid' but needs more time.
The Witch's Brew holiday edition that drove the Q4 2024 spike will be re-launched in Q4 2025 - a near-term scanner-data/revenue catalyst.

Adjacent categories: protein is interesting (a growing segment, under analysis with potential to build out); stick packs a big on-the-go opportunity and a profitable piece of the business; some other inherited products under evaluation per internal profitability algorithms; near-term focus is RTD energy.

Marketing synergies come from 'marketing operations' - scale media buys and crossover/shared resources - not from merging the creative/brand teams; the portfolio gives flexibility to dial in innovation timing across channels.

~$10.7M distributor termination fees relate to Alani switching distributors before the acquisition (notification period plus a multiple of gross profit); no update on the go-forward distributor network - focus is integration and existing customers/partners.
Alani Nu currently distributed internationally only through Canada, with other countries 'in the pipeline.'

Separate brand teams handle creative, social and brand voice; synergies come from 'marketing operations' - scale media buys and crossover/shared resources (e.g., field-marketing resources). Managing a portfolio in one category lets the company dial in innovation timing to maximize the retailer/channel footprint, giving flexibility the company lacked before the Alani Nu acquisition and enabling appropriate fund allocation on a consistent timeline.
David Shakno, William Blair (for Jon Andersen)
Whether the non-energy mix at Alani Nu (sticks, shakes, snacks) should persist, given some of those categories are incremental to legacy Celsius.

The broader adjacent-category portfolio is interesting - protein is a growing segment under further analysis with potential to build out; stick packs offer a big on-the-go opportunity (Celsius has seen stick-pack growth) leveraging Celsius's sales organization and supply chain, and a profitable piece of the business. Some other inherited products are under evaluation per internal profitability algorithms. Near-term, the company is extremely focused on RTD energy where it sees immediate accretive synergies through the back half of 2025 and into 2026.
Who received the ~$10.7M distributor termination fees and whether there is any update on the distributor network plan.

The fees relate to Alani Nu switching distributors before the acquisition - typically a notification period and a multiple of gross profit paid when leaving certain distributors for others - activity that occurred prior to Celsius acquiring Alani Nu as it updated its distribution platform. The company is focused on integrating Alani Nu and the organization and on existing customers/partners, with no distributor-network update at this time.
